units.zh: 十一月，安祿山據范陽叛。
units.en: In the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled from Fanyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month An Lushan seized Fanyang and rebelled.

units.zh: 十三日，祿山陷東京，常清以餘眾奔陜州，謂仙芝曰：「累日血戰，賊鋒不可當。
units.en: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his survivors to Shanzhou and told Xianzhi, "We have fought for days in blood — the rebel host cannot be stopped.
units.literal: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his remaining troops to Shanzhou and said to Xianzhi: "For days we have fought in blood; the rebels' spearhead cannot be withstood.

units.zh: 平盧軍節度使侯希逸引兵保青州，授青密節度使，遂廢淄沂節度，並所管五州，號淄青平盧節度，增領齊州。
units.en: Pinglu Army military commissioner Hou Xiyi led his troops to hold Qingzhou and was appointed Qing–Mi military commissioner; the Zi–Yi circuit was then abolished and its five prefectures absorbed into the newly styled Zi–Qing–Pinglu circuit, which also gained Qi Prefecture.
units.literal: The Pinglu Army military commissioner Hou Xiyi led troops to hold Qingzhou; he was appointed Qing-Mi military commissioner, whereupon the Zi-Yi circuit was abolished and its five prefectures were merged in, styled the Zi-Qing-Pinglu circuit, and Qi Prefecture was added to its jurisdiction.

units.zh: 761 二年 置滑衛節度使，治滑州，領州六：滑、衛、相、魏、德、貝。
units.en: In 761, the second year of Shangyuan, a Hua–Wei military commissioner was created at Hua Prefecture, commanding Hua, Wei, Xiang, Wei, De, and Bei.
units.literal: 761, second year. The Hua-Wei military commissioner was established, with seat at Hua Prefecture, holding six prefectures: Hua, Wei, Xiang, Wei, De, and Bei.

units.zh: 事未行，會赦王廷湊，諸道班師。
units.en: Before the plan could be enacted, Wang Tingcou was pardoned and the allied armies withdrew.
units.literal: Before the matter could be carried out, there came an amnesty for Wang Tingcou; the various circuits withdrew their armies.

units.zh: 初，同捷狂桀犯命，濟之以王廷湊，王師經年無功。
units.en: At first Tongjie's wild defiance of orders was sustained by aid from Wang Tingcou, and the imperial armies had failed for years.
units.literal: At first Tongjie was wild and defiant in offending orders; he was aided by Wang Tingcou; the imperial army for years had no success.

units.zh: 時李寶臣卒於其位，子惟嶽匿喪求位，上遣宏使成德問疾，且喻之。
units.en: When regional strongman Li Baochen died in office, his son Wei Yue hid the death to seize power. The emperor dispatched Ban Hong to Chengde under the pretense of a condolence visit to warn him against it.
units.literal: At the time Li Baochen died in office; his son Wei Yue concealed the funeral seeking succession; the emperor sent Hong as envoy to Chengde to inquire after illness and instruct him.

units.zh: 十年，領朔方靈鹽節度大使、靈州大都督，以朔方行軍司馬李欒為靈府左司馬，知府事，朔方留後。
units.en: In the tenth year, he was named military commissioner of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan and Grand Governor of Lingzhou; Li Luan, campaign vice commander of Shuofang, was appointed left vice commander of Ling prefecture, managed prefectural affairs, and served as Shuofang deputy commissioner.
units.literal: In the tenth year, he took charge as military commissioner of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan and Grand Governor of Lingzhou; Li Luan, campaign vice commander of Shuofang, was made left vice commander of Ling prefecture, managed prefectural affairs, and served as Shuofang deputy commissioner.

units.zh: 群臣袁盎等諫說雖切，常假借納用焉。
units.en: His ministers Yuan Ang and others offered blunt remonstrances, but he always accepted and employed them through tactful accommodation.
units.literal: His ministers Yuan Ang and others offered remonstrances that were cutting, but he always accepted and employed them through accommodation.

units.zh: 會於頔、杜黃裳家私事發，連逮鑒虛下獄。
units.en: When private scandals at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.
units.literal: When private affairs at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.

units.zh: 初，以柳公綽在鎮無功，議將代之，裴度言：「道古嗣曹王皋之子，皋嘗以江漢兵遏希烈之亂，威惠至今在人，復用其子必能繼美。」
units.en: When Liu Gongchuo's tenure had yielded no results, the court considered replacing him. Pei Du argued, "Li Daogu is the son of Prince of Cao Li Gao. Li Gao once held the Jiang-Han line against Li Xilie's rebellion, and his prestige and kindness are remembered to this day. Appointing his son would carry on that legacy."
units.literal: Initially, because Liu Gongchuo at his post had no achievements, there was discussion of replacing him; Pei Du said: "Daogu is heir as son of Prince of Cao Gao; Gao once with Jiang-Han troops checked Xi Lie's rebellion; prestige and kindness remain in people's hearts to this day; employing his son again will surely be able to continue the excellence."

units.zh: 會橫海節度使李祐平德州，同捷窮，請降，祐使大將萬洪代守滄州，同捷未出也，耆以三百騎馳入滄，以事誅洪，與同捷朝京師。
units.en: Li You of Transverse Sea took Dezhou; Tongjie, desperate, offered to yield. You left Wan Hong to hold Cangzhou while Tongjie lingered; Ji raced in with three hundred riders, killed Hong, and brought Tongjie to court.
units.literal: When Transverse Sea military commissioner Li You pacified Dezhou, Tongjie was cornered and sought surrender; You had great general Wan Hong hold Cangzhou in his stead while Tongjie had not yet departed. Ji galloped into Cang with three hundred horsemen, executed Hong on the facts of the case, and escorted Tongjie to the capital.

units.zh: 初，祐聞耆殺洪，大驚，疾遂劇。
units.en: When You first heard Ji had killed Hong, he was stunned and his illness worsened.
units.literal: Earlier, when You heard Ji had killed Hong, he was greatly shocked and his illness grew severe.

units.zh: 帝曰：「祐若死，是耆殺之。」
units.en: The emperor said, "If You dies, Ji has killed him."
units.literal: The emperor said: "If You dies, it is Ji who killed him."

units.zh: 然暴橫少恩，杖前部尉以逞憾，觀察使王緯以聞，德宗不省。
units.en: Yet he was brutal and unforgiving: he had a former subordinate commandant flogged to settle a personal score. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported it, but Emperor Dezong paid no heed.
units.literal: Yet he was violent and overbearing and short on kindness; he beat a former subordinate commandant to vent a grudge. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported this, but Emperor Dezong took no notice.

units.zh: 帝晚務姑息，頔所奏建，無不開允。
units.en: In his later years the emperor favored appeasement, and every proposal Di submitted won approval.
units.literal: The emperor in his later years pursued indulgence and forbearance; whatever Di memorialized and proposed was invariably approved.

units.zh: 俄擅以兵取鄧州，天子未始誰何。
units.en: Before long he seized Dengzhou by force on his own authority, and the emperor never called him to account.
units.literal: Soon he on his own authority took Dengzhou by force, and the Son of Heaven never once held him to account.

units.zh: 智興能駛步，奉表，不數日至京師告急，德宗出朔方軍五千擊納，解去，自是為徐特將。
units.en: Zhixing could run at great speed; he carried a memorial and reached the capital within days to report the crisis. Dezong dispatched five thousand Shuofang troops against Na and lifted the siege; from then on Zhixing was a special general of Xuzhou.
units.literal: Zhixing could run swiftly; he bore a memorial and in only a few days reached the capital to report the emergency. Dezong sent out five thousand Shuofang troops to strike Na, and the siege was lifted; from then on he was a special general of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 德宗既厭兵，大抵刺史重代易，至歷年不徙。
units.en: After the emperor wearied of campaigning, prefects were usually turned over often—though some lingered in office for years on end.
units.literal: Once Emperor Dezong grew weary of warfare, for the most part prefects were frequently rotated, yet some went years without transfer.

units.zh: 德宗立，召還。
units.en: Dezong's accession brought his recall to court.
units.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was recalled.

units.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。
units.en: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, Hongzheng left Wei to assume command of Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhen prefecture died; Hongzheng moved from Wei to take charge of Zhen.

units.zh: 二年六月六日，賊將史思明自范陽來救，戰於安陽河北，王師不利，炅中流矢奔退。
units.en: On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, Shi Siming marched from Fanyang to relieve the siege. The armies clashed north of the Anyang River. The imperial side faltered; Jiong took an arrow wound and withdrew.
units.literal: On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, the rebel general Shi Siming came from Fanyang to relieve the city; they fought north of the Anyang River; the imperial army was at a disadvantage; Jiong was struck by an arrow and fled.

units.zh: 王鍔死，家奴告鍔子稷易父奏末，冒遺獻。
units.en: After Wang E died, a household slave accused his son Ji of tampering with the end of his father's final memorial and presenting it as a posthumous petition.
units.literal: When Wang E died, a household slave reported that E's son Ji had altered the end of his father's memorial and falsely presented it as a posthumous submission.

units.zh: 遠祖沒諾幹，唐至德中，事鎮州節度使王武俊為騎將。
units.en: His distant ancestor Mo Nuogan served as a cavalry commander under Wang Wujun, military governor of Zhenzhou, during the Zhide reign of Tang.
units.literal: A remote ancestor, Mo Nuogan, during the Zhide era of Tang served the Zhenzhou military governor Wang Wujun as a mounted commander.

units.zh: 武俊嘉其勇幹，畜為假子，號王五哥，其後子孫以王為氏。
units.en: Wujun admired his courage and competence, took him as an adoptive son, and called him Fifth Brother Wang; his descendants thereafter adopted Wang as their clan surname.
units.literal: Wujun admired his courage and ability, raised him as an adopted son, and called him Fifth Brother Wang; later generations took Wang as their surname.

units.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
units.en: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng ahead with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the Yellow River and take one fortified camp after another.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to cross the river with four thousand vanguard troops, repeatedly capturing his fortified camps.

units.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。
units.en: Jintao had settled in Wei as an outsider, pledged himself to the army, and served under the military governor Tian Hongzheng.
units.literal: Jintao lived as a guest in Wei, pledged himself to the army gate, and served the military governor Tian Hongzheng.

units.zh: 居數月，爲王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。
units.en: Within a few months Hongzheng was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.
units.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then rebelled with troops.

units.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布爲魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。
units.en: The court made Hongzheng's son Bu military governor of Weibo and sent him to campaign against the rebels, that he might avenge his father's death.
units.literal: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu as military governor of Weibo and led troops to punish the rebels, so that he might avenge his father.

units.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔爲衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。
units.en: When Hongzheng marched on Yanzhou by imperial order and broke Li Shidao, Jintao was chief controller of horse and foot in the headquarters guard and was made concurrent Attending Censor for his service.
units.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to campaign against Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, and for his merit was appointed concurrent Attending Censor.

units.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。
units.en: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the garrison city and memorialized for the commander's seal and baton, whereupon the court mobilized an army against him.
units.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the military city by stealth, memorialized requesting the seal and baton of command, and the court raised troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉爲助。
units.en: Xiancheng had earlier been linked to Quanlue by marriage; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly supplied him with grain and fodder.
units.literal: Earlier Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly aided him with provisions.

units.zh: 溫固執，文宗諭而止。
units.en: Wei held firm until Wenzong instructed him to stop.
units.literal: Wei persisted; Emperor Wenzong instructed him and he desisted.

units.zh: 開成初，文宗欲以真源、臨真二公主降士族，謂宰相曰：「民間脩婚姻，不計官品而上閥閱。
units.en: Early in Kaicheng, Wenzong meant to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen into great clans and told his chief ministers: "Common folk arranging marriages care nothing for office and everything for pedigree.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, Emperor Wenzong wished to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen to gentry families and said to the chief ministers: "Among the people in arranging marriages, they do not consider official rank but esteem clan pedigree.

units.zh: 帝聞異之，轉太仆、衛尉二少卿，歷左右金吾大將軍。
units.en: The emperor, struck by his words, moved him through the vice directorships of the Stud and Guard courts and then the Left and Right commands of the Golden Guard.
units.literal: The emperor heard this with surprise and transferred him to the two vice directorships of the Court of the Imperial Stud and the Court of the Imperial Guard, then through the Left and Right Golden Guard commands.

units.zh: 久之，復拜司農卿，入謝，帝曰：「卿用法深，信乎？」
units.en: Long afterward he was reappointed Director of the National Granaries; at his audience of thanks the emperor asked, "They say you enforce the law harshly—is it true?"
units.literal: After a long while he was again appointed Director of the Court of the National Granaries; entering to give thanks, the emperor said: "You apply the law with severity—is that so?"

units.zh: 帝許之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: The emperor consented.
